title: 0002 coverage: artifact families, save versions and pylavi decoding in prepared sources
body:
## Goal
Measure, from the prepared public sources only, which LabVIEW artifact families and save versions are present and which resource types pylavi decodes. Report, do not fix: do not patch pylavi or write a reader.

Iterations 0000 and 0001 ordered this work and no output was produced. Commit the script and a first partial report early (within the first third of the session), then extend it.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `docs/research/scripts/coverage/inventory.py` runs offline with `python3 -I` against `$LABVIEW_ENVIRONMENT` and prints a JSON inventory: per file extension/artifact family, the file count and the set of save versions read from file headers.
- [ ] `docs/research/0002-coverage.md` contains a table of artifact families x save versions with counts, produced by that script (the command used is quoted).
- [ ] The report lists, for the fixture `Core/ActorFramework/Actor/Actor Core.vi` and at least one file of every other family found, which resource types pylavi decodes and which it leaves opaque, citing pylavi source paths under `@environment/`.
- [ ] A `## Gaps` section lists missing families, missing versions, block diagrams that are not decodable, and license/dependency limits, each as a visible gap (not an exclusion).
- [ ] Every factual claim cites a file path under `@environment/` or the script output.

## Verification
`python3 -I docs/research/scripts/coverage/inventory.py`

## Context
- `@environment/readiness.json`: pinned pylavi `35d2a03` and Actor Framework `371c631`, fixture hash, 30 resource types; start here.
- `docs/perpetua/evaluation.md`: coverage must be reported per artifact family and version; gaps stay visible.
- `journal/0001.md` `## State`: what is already known and what is not.

## Budget
- `@environment/readiness.json`
- `@environment/` pylavi and actor-framework trees
- `docs/perpetua/evaluation.md`
- `journal/0001.md`

title: 0002 delivery: compare delivery options and estimate all-versions vs 2024-only effort
body:
## Goal
Compare technical delivery options for letting AI agents read LabVIEW artifacts like ordinary code (CLI text export, Python library, MCP server, committed text mirror) against the goal, and estimate the effort of supporting all LabVIEW versions versus a LabVIEW 2024-only fallback, with the compatibility limits of each. Report, do not decide: the owner chooses; make no fallback choice.

Iterations 0000 and 0001 ordered this work and no output was produced. Commit a first partial report early (within the first third of the session), then extend it.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `docs/research/0002-delivery.md` exists with one section per option (CLI export, Python library, MCP server, committed text mirror): how an agent uses it, what it needs at runtime, offline/licensing constraints, and which artifact families it can serve.
- [ ] A section `## Effort: all versions vs 2024-only` gives an estimate for each variant as ranges with stated assumptions, and lists the version-format differences that drive the difference, each citing a source path under `@environment/` (for example pylavi version handling) or marking the claim as unverified.
- [ ] A section `## Compatibility limits of the 2024 fallback` lists what a 2024-only tool would not read.
- [ ] A section `## Open measurements` turns each unverified claim into a concrete measurement a later task could run.
- [ ] The report states explicitly that it makes no choice for the owner.

## Verification
`python3 -I -c "import pathlib,sys; t=pathlib.Path('docs/research/0002-delivery.md').read_text(); req=['## Effort: all versions vs 2024-only','## Compatibility limits of the 2024 fallback','## Open measurements','MCP','CLI']; m=[r for r in req if r not in t]; print('missing:',m); sys.exit(1 if m else 0)"`

## Context
- `docs/perpetua/roles.md`: work sequence step 1; compare delivery options including MCP rather than choosing for the owner.
- `@environment/readiness.json`: what is prepared; pylavi is the only prepared parser.
- `journal/0001.md` `## State`: fallback decision is the owner's, after this estimate.

## Budget
- `docs/perpetua/roles.md`
- `@environment/readiness.json`
- `@environment/` pylavi tree
- `journal/0001.md`

title: 0002 benchmark sources milestone: pinned source provenance
body:
## Goal
Complete the benchmark `sources` milestone from `docs/perpetua/evaluation.md`: a reproducible, offline record of which prepared public sources the benchmark may use, with their pins, licenses and hashes. Preparation only: do not write tasks, oracle answers or product code, and do not approve your own readiness.

Iterations 0000 and 0001 ordered this work and no output was produced. Commit the script and a first `benchmark/sources.json` early (within the first third of the session), then extend it.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `benchmark/scripts/sources.py` runs offline with `python3 -I` against `$LABVIEW_ENVIRONMENT`, regenerates `benchmark/sources.json`, and exits nonzero if any recorded hash or pin differs from the prepared files.
- [ ] `benchmark/sources.json` lists each source repository (name, upstream URL, commit, license) and each LabVIEW artifact file used (path, sha256, size, save version from header).
- [ ] `benchmark/sources.md` explains provenance, states that all sources are public and therefore cannot serve as withheld or unseen cases, and lists missing sources as visible gaps.
- [ ] `benchmark/preparation.json` records the milestone `sources` as prepared-not-reviewed, with the generating command, and every other milestone of evaluation.md as not started.

## Verification
`python3 -I benchmark/scripts/sources.py --check`

## Context
- `docs/perpetua/evaluation.md`: authoritative readiness contract and milestone list.
- `@environment/readiness.json`: pins, licenses and fixture hash to start from.
- `docs/perpetua/roles.md`: benchmark authors do not approve their own readiness; public examples cannot be claimed unseen.

## Budget
- `docs/perpetua/evaluation.md`
- `docs/perpetua/roles.md`
- `@environment/readiness.json`
- `@environment/` pylavi and actor-framework trees
